correctness.rationale: With b>=2 and the exact synchronous 0->1->2->0 threshold rule, traceback from an excitation at time t branches at least b ways. Excitations at the same site cannot be two ticks apart, so backwards paths never immediately retrace an edge; on a tree they are simple and siblings' branches cannot meet. A height-t witness therefore takes at least (b^(t+1)-1)/(b-1) vertices. This forces t<=h, and a height-h witness spans and is rooted at the true root (any other vertex is farther than h from a leaf in a different first-generation branch). Its time labels force bottom states 1,0,{0,2}. Conversely the first two updates produce the waves as stated (the parent alone cannot stimulate a nonleaf with b>=2). If all children fire at j-1, none fires at j-2 or j-3. For j>=3 their parent cannot fire at either j-2 or j-1; it must be at rest at j-1 regardless of the initial state and external parent trajectory. It fires at j. The last excitation at h is nonzero through h+1 and is gone by h+2; if no excitation occurs at h, extinction is by h+1. The product count, probability and h=0,1 cases follow directly. My independent simulator checked both extinction time and the predicted extremizer predicate coordinatewise for every enumerated initial state, including all 3^15 binary height-three states (12 maximizers), all 3^13 ternary height-two states (2), and the ternary height-three slice with leaves fixed (24). Replay: python3 /workspace/reviews/reproduce.py 4 full (NumPy); /workspace/reviews/reproduce-output.txt. The height-three ternary slice is not full enumeration; the proof covers all parameters. Frozen C++/Python and saved outputs were inspected, not executed.
